fulltext: Samsung Newsroom
on November 16, 2026

From a Victory Selfie debut to technology integrations and immersive experiences in the Youth Olympic Village, Samsung brought mobile innovation into the heart of Africa’s first Olympic sporting event

The Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 opened in Senegal on October 31, giving young athletes a defining stage to test their limits and grow on and off the field. As a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, Samsung Electronics has been a constant force behind that journey — bringing Galaxy technology to medal ceremonies, competition venues, and the Youth Olympic Village to help future Olympians make the most of their first global spotlight.

At Africa’s first Olympic sporting event, that commitment took shape across the podium, competition venues and the Youth Olympic Village. Athletes used Galaxy to capture their own celebrations on the podium, while Galaxy devices brought the action closer to fans through broadcast coverage. In the Village, the technology gave athletes ways to express themselves and make memories with new friends. Together, these experiences helped them capture, share, and connect throughout their time at the Games.

Standing on the Olympic podium represents years of dedication and sacrifice. While that moment had traditionally been captured through official photography, the Olympic Victory Selfie had established a new tradition at the Olympic Games since its introduction at Paris 2024 — one where athletes captured the celebration using mobile devices.

At Dakar 2026, Samsung brought Victory Selfie to the Youth Olympic Games for the first time, letting young athletes standing on their first Olympic podium capture the emotion themselves. Captured with Galaxy Z Flip7 Olympic Edition device, these podium moments are being shared with family, friends, and supporters around the world.

Beyond the podium, Samsung also explored how Galaxy could bring fans closer to the competition itself. Galaxy S26 Ultra devices were integrated into skateboarding and taekwondo coverage, capturing dynamic perspectives alongside traditional broadcast cameras. Building on previous Games-time integrations, Dakar 2026 marked a step beyond ceremonial moments into fast-paced competition — testing how smartphones can complement production workflows.

Galaxy S26 Ultra was also used to create social content. Footage from skateboarding, gymnastics, and athletics was captured as a series of vertical videos optimized for social platforms and shared through IOC social channels, bringing the energy of the Games to athletes and fans.

“Our collaboration with Samsung at previous Olympic Games, including Paris 2024 and Milano Cortina 2026, has shown how mobile technology can bring new experiences to Olympic viewers. At Dakar 2026, we continued to build on this collaboration, with the integration of Galaxy S26 Ultra devices further demonstrating their potential value in our visual storytelling,” said Mark Wallace, Olympic Broadcasting Services Chief Production Officer. “The insights gained will help inform our ongoing exploration of innovative production ideas as we look ahead to LA28, where emerging technologies can further enrich Olympic coverage and create more immersive experiences for viewers.”

While competition brought young athletes to Dakar 2026, the moments between events offered a chance to connect with people from different countries and cultures. Inside the Youth Olympic Village, Samsung Open Station gave them a place to step away from competition, express their creativity and build friendships through Galaxy technology.

Athletes created Olympic-themed characters and posters at the Victory Wall and captured memories with selfies at the Victory Photo Zone. At Victory Talk, they recorded video messages about their experiences in Dakar and their hopes for the future.
In the Community Lounge, athletes played mobile games, made personalized keychains, and explored Galaxy features through Galaxy Tips, finding natural ways to connect across nationalities and sports.

“I really enjoyed Samsung Open Station and how interactive it is. There are so many ways to make memories and create things to take back home,” said Team Cook Islands swimmer Alicia Story. “The Victory Wall was my favorite part because you can see all the different perspectives of athletes from across the world and how they create their characters and show their personalities.”

Two-time Olympic street skateboarding medalist and Paris 2024 Team Samsung Galaxy member Rayssa Leal visited Samsung Open Station as a Dakar 2026 Athlete Role Model and Global Ambassador, meeting young athletes and exploring the Galaxy experiences onsite.

Samsung will build on its experience at Dakar 2026 as it continues its technology collaborations toward the LA28 Games, helping athletes and fans connect more closely and share in the excitement of the Olympic Games.

“At Dakar 2026, we wanted Galaxy technology to be part of the moments young athletes would actually remember — whether they were competing, celebrating, meeting new people, or simply spending time together in the Village,” said Sophia Kim, Vice President and Head of Experience Marketing Group, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics. “We’re proud to have supported this historic Games and to take what we learned in Dakar 2026 forward as we continue our Olympic journey toward the LA28 Games.”

fulltext_cn: 三星新闻中心
从胜利自拍首次亮相到青奥村的技术集成和沉浸式体验，三星将移动创新带入非洲首届奥运会体育赛事的核心
2026 年达喀尔青奥会于 10 月 31 日在塞内加尔开幕，为年轻运动员提供了一个考验极限、在赛场内外成长的决定性舞台。作为奥运会和残奥会的全球合作伙伴，三星电子一直是这一历程背后的持续力量——将 Galaxy 技术带到奖牌仪式、比赛场馆和青奥村，帮助未来的奥运会选手充分利用他们的首次全球聚光灯。
在非洲首届奥运会体育赛事中，这一承诺在领奖台、比赛场馆和青奥村中得到体现。运动员使用 Galaxy 捕捉自己在领奖台上的庆祝动作，而 Galaxy 设备则通过广播报道拉近了球迷与赛事的距离。在村里，这项技术为运动员提供了表达自己并与新朋友留下回忆的方式。这些经历共同帮助他们在奥运会期间捕捉、分享和联系。
站在奥林匹克领奖台上代表着多年的奉献和牺牲。虽然这一时刻传统上是通过官方摄影来捕捉的，但自 2024 年巴黎奥运会推出以来，奥运胜利自拍在奥运会上建立了一个新的传统——运动员使用移动设备捕捉庆祝活动。
在2026年达喀尔，三星首次将胜利自拍带入青奥会，让年轻运动员首次登上奥运会领奖台，捕捉激动人心的瞬间。这些登上领奖台的时刻是由 Galaxy Z Flip7 奥运版设备捕捉到的，并与世界各地的家人、朋友和支持者分享。
除了领奖台之外，三星还探索了 Galaxy 如何让粉丝更接近比赛本身。 Galaxy S26 Ultra 设备被集成到滑板和跆拳道报道中，与传统广播摄像机一起捕捉动态视角。在之前的奥运会期间整合的基础上，2026 年达喀尔奥运会标志着从仪式时刻迈入快节奏的竞争——测试智能手机如何补充生产工作流程。
Galaxy S26 Ultra 还被用来创建社交内容。滑板、体操、田径等项目的视频被捕捉为一系列针对社交平台优化的垂直视频，并通过国际奥委会社交渠道进行分享，为运动员和球迷带来了奥运会的能量。

奥林匹克广播服务首席制作官 Mark Wallace 表示：“我们在往届奥运会（包括 2024 年巴黎奥运会和 2026 年米兰科尔蒂纳奥运会）上与三星的合作，展示了移动技术如何为奥运会观众带来新的体验。在 2026 年达喀尔奥运会上，我们继续深化这一合作，Galaxy S26 Ultra 设备的集成进一步展示了它们在我们视觉故事讲述中的潜在价值。” “在展望 LA28 时，所获得的见解将有助于我们不断探索创新制作理念，其中新兴技术可以进一步丰富奥运会报道，并为观众创造更身临其境的体验。”
虽然比赛让年轻运动员来到 2026 年达喀尔，但赛事之间的时刻也提供了与来自不同国家和文化的人们建立联系的机会。在青奥村内，三星开放站为他们提供了一个远离竞争、表达创造力并通过 Galaxy 技术建立友谊的场所。
运动员们在胜利墙创作了奥运主题的人物和海报，并在胜利拍照区用自拍照捕捉了美好回忆。在胜利演讲中，他们录制了视频信息，讲述了他们在达喀尔的经历以及对未来的希望。
在社区休息室，运动员们玩手机游戏、制作个性化钥匙扣，并通过 Galaxy Tips 探索 Galaxy 功能，找到跨民族和跨运动的自然联系方式。
“我真的很喜欢三星开放站及其互动性。有很多方法可以留下回忆并创造一些东西带回家，”库克群岛游泳运动员艾丽西亚·斯托里 (Alicia Story) 说道。 “胜利墙是我最喜欢的部分，因为你可以看到世界各地运动员的不同视角，以及他们如何塑造自己的角色并展示他们的个性。”
两届奥运会街头滑板奖牌得主、巴黎 2024 年三星 Galaxy 队成员 Rayssa Leal 作为 2026 年达喀尔运动员榜样和全球大使访问了三星公开站，与年轻运动员会面并在现场探索 Galaxy 体验。
三星将借鉴 2026 年达喀尔的经验，继续与 LA28 奥运会进行技术合作，帮助运动员和球迷更紧密地联系并分享奥运会的兴奋。
三星电子移动体验 (MX) 业务副总裁兼体验营销集团负责人 Sophia Kim 表示：“在 2026 年达喀尔，我们希望 Galaxy 技术成为年轻运动员真正记住的时刻的一部分，无论他们是在比赛、庆祝、结识新朋友，还是只是在达喀尔村共度时光。” “我们很自豪能够支持这一历史性的奥运会，并将我们在 2026 年达喀尔所学到的知识继续发扬光大，继续我们的奥运之旅，迈向洛杉矶 28 届奥运会。”

cards.title: App+1｜不卡带：给你爱听的「老调」，配点记忆中的风味
cards.summary: 能切换老设备音质的媒体播放器。 查看全文
fulltext: Matrix 首页推荐
Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。
文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。
App 是 AI 写的，但文章是手打的，可以放心食用。App 名字叫做《不卡带》，是个界面老登、音质低清的本地音频播放器。
什么人会对这个感兴趣（我猜的）？
《不卡带》没有太多奇思妙想和创意，只是一种对于现代 UI 习惯的一种叛逆。起初是我拿到公司的测试机——一台 vivo X Flip——随便把玩时出来的想法，这手机型号也好几年了，平时放着就测试 app 时会打开一下。作为一款现在已经不算新的小折叠屏，一般来说我连翻开内屏的想法都没有。
刚好前段时间下载了一整套十几年前《游戏城寨》赠送 CD 里转制的 MP3，之前每一期杂志我都买，但大学毕业后连书带盘都不见了。我就想找一个小的 MP3 播放器，做个睡前或工作时的听歌设备。它只有外放就好，不用太大声，也不需要多么高清。
vivo X Flip 折叠后四四方方的很小巧，似乎就是一个不错的选择。
vivo X Flip 还和别的折叠屏不一样：应用要在外屏打开，还要专门接入「魔镜应用」。那干脆就给这个小屏 vibe 一个能播放本地音乐的 app 吧。
在我最初的想法里，一个 MP3 播放器 app 做起来肯定不会费太多事（算力），随便一个 agent 帮着做了就行。趁还订阅着 Gogole AI Pro，我直接用 Antigravity 开工。那时还是 10 月 20 号。

经常 vibe 的朋友都知道，AI 能帮你几分钟做出 80% 的功能需求，剩下要达到预期效果，就不是几小时甚至几天能完善好的了。在不断修改增加功能、做适配、抠 UI 细节时，没几天 Antigravity 的大模型用量跑完了，又开始用 Codex 接手。做完 vivo X Flip 外屏可用了，又想适配手上的 moto Razr 50 Ultra，接着手上的 OPPO Find N2 似乎也能发挥余热。折叠屏适配完了，我又薅到一台 Nothing Phone 4a Pro……
截至本文发布，这款 App 已经基本可用，所以拿出来给大家试试，听听意见。（其实一个原因是今天看到 x 上有人推 Duo 上的应用 Duoamp，同样是仿 WinAMP 界面的应用）
《不卡带》可以播放主流格式的音频和视频文件，播放视频时（这个功能聊胜于无，但放放 MV 感觉还不错）可以在封面区域预览且支持双击放大，除了手机本地的媒体文件，也可以通过 WebDAV 连接 NAS，将媒体文件导入到播放列表实现「在线听歌」。
应用也支持快速切换多种 EQ 场景，在 Fold 手机上可以方便地调整均衡器：
设计这边，《不卡带》采用了复古风格的播放器界面，主界面由金属外壳和液晶屏组成，你可以直接导入 https://skins.webamp.org/ 的皮肤使用（并没充分测试，偶尔某个皮肤可能适配得很好）；针对 moto Razr 50 Ultra 外屏凸起的双摄像头，我在界面上额外做了两个旋钮，双指捏住摄像头转动可以调节音量和 noise。
《不卡带》也有一套主题制作的规范，你可以自己写或者让 AI 帮你画，打包导入 App 使用。
至于 Noise filters 功能，它可以让你快速切换具有不同风味的实体复古设备音质效果，如：
以上是我脑补的，感兴趣可以自行安装验证😄。Noise 的音量可调，滤镜搭配不同场景 EQ，不同歌曲可以获得完全不同的收听感受。播放同一首歌的时候连续切换设备滤镜，你会很直观地听出某种设备相较其他设备的独特质感。
对我个人来说，我比较喜欢在睡觉前把折叠手机合上，小小一个放在枕头边上，外放声音不用很大，配合 VINYL 或者 RADIO 的声音滤镜，播放上世纪的老歌，身心都很治愈。
一个人工作时，播放《游戏城寨》CD 的 MP3，有编辑的介绍、有小时候熟悉的游戏主题曲，配上略带沙沙声的 TAPE 噪音，不失为一种享受。
《不卡带》已在 vivo 应用商城上架，只当做一次隐私与合规的检验，所以版本更新较慢。如果你感兴趣，我更推荐从这里下载安装。

Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents.

At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world.

Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage.

“It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.”

The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system.

More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean. Workshops covered deploying and optimizing AI inference at scale, building end-to-end robotics workflows with the NVIDIA Isaac platform and developing secure AI agents. Certification included the new AI Model and Application Development exam.

The Physical AI Startup Connect event included pitches from 10 NVIDIA Inception startups: AIM Intelligence, Avikus, GoLe Robotics, MOVIN, Neubility, ROAI, ROBROS, TESOLLO, TwelveLabs and XYZ. The AI for Science Forum brought together the Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information, Korean universities and NVIDIA Research.
AI Day Seoul sessions will soon be available on NVIDIA On-Demand.

Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

The New Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview.
“Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor told TechCrunch.

Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup’s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision.

Bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system.

The startup’s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers’ hands by the end of 2027.

The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market.

Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its American operations, which span engineering and business development in Santa Clara. The startup plans to increase its U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027, Kapoor said. It has also begun hiring engineers in Europe.
“It’s a story of can we build a global technology company out of India,” Kapoor said.

In 2024, Bharat Semi announced plans for a semiconductor fabrication project in India involving a technology partnership with the U.S. Space Force. The initiative, Kapoor said, remains in development and the startup is working to identify domestic partners that would build and operate the facility.

The project is separate from Bharat Semi’s image-sensor business, Kapoor added. The startup plans to remain fabless, outsourcing chip manufacturing while focusing on semiconductor design and software. The new funding will not be used to finance the proposed fabrication facility.

这项投资是在这家成立近五年、尚未实现营收的初创公司表示，它已获得美国国防技术公司通用原子公司和印度凯恩斯半导体公司的设计胜利之际进行的。然而，其图像传感器仍在开发中，该初创公司的目标是在 2027 年进行首次商业生产。
印度已投入数十亿美元建设国内半导体产业，希望在美国公司寻求中国以外的供应链多元化之际成为替代制造中心。然而，该国尚未将自己打造为主要的芯片制造中心。与此同时，人工智能的繁荣也为 Bharat Semi 等印度初创公司提供了为全球市场开发专用芯片的机会。
这家总部位于新德里的初创公司正在开发可编程图像传感器，将图像捕获、处理和人工智能功能结合在单个芯片上，从而减少将视觉数据发送到单独处理器的需要。联合创始人 Vrinda Kapoor（上图右）在接受采访时表示，与使用独立图像传感器、图像信号处理器和片上系统的传统设置相比，此举可以将系统成本降低至少 70%。
“我们的目标是从传感器转向感知解决方案，”卡普尔告诉 TechCrunch。
卡普尔是南方公园下议院研究员，此前曾在医疗保健技术领域工作过，他于 2021 年底与该初创公司董事总经理 Vinayak Dalmia（上图左）共同创立了 Bharat Semi，后者曾在麦肯锡和私募股权部门工作过。其首席技术官博伊德·福勒 (Boyd Fowler) 此前曾在图像传感器制造商 OmniVision 担任过相同职务。
Bharat Semi 的目标市场是智能家居、工业自动化、监控和航空航天。卡普尔没有透露具体细节，他指出空调可以检测房间何时空并自动调整，无人机也可以处理视觉信息——即使系统中其他地方没有更昂贵的计算硬件。
Kapoor 表示，该初创公司的第一代传感器已经进入原型设计阶段，而其第二代传感器将融入更先进的人工智能功能，预计将于 2027 年中期进入原型阶段。此外，该初创公司计划在 2027 年底前将这些更新的传感器交付给客户。
全股权种子轮融资由 Info Edge Group、South Park Commons 和 Indus Bridge Ventures 领投，Valor Capital、Micromax、Gaingels 和个人投资者跟投。卡普尔表示，Bharat Semi 计划利用这笔资金扩大其工程团队、完成产品开发并将其传感器推向市场。
Bharat Semi 在印度和美国拥有约 75 名员工，其中 10 至 12 名员工在其美国业务部门，负责圣克拉拉的工程和业务开发。 Kapoor 表示，该初创公司计划到 2027 年中期将其美国员工人数增加到 20 人左右。它还开始在欧洲招聘工程师。
卡普尔说：“这是一个关于我们能否在印度建立一家全球科技公司的故事。”
2024 年，Bharat Semi 宣布计划在印度开展半导体制造项目，涉及与美国太空军的技术合作。卡普尔表示，该计划仍在开发中，该初创公司正在努力寻找建造和运营该设施的国内合作伙伴。
卡普尔补充说，该项目与 Bharat Semi 的图像传感器业务是分开的。该初创公司计划保持无晶圆厂，外包芯片制造，同时专注于半导体设计和软件。新资金将不会用于资助拟议的制造设施。

We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.”
“Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.”

Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return.) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem.
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here.
Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days.

Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned.
But someone said to me, “If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down

Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. I mean, no one is quite as special as Elon is, but it’s a big, incredibly successful company. Like you said — in a lot of ways, the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia.

And for most people, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. He’s the biggest shareholder. He has family members who work at the company, and probably most importantly, there was no succession plan in place. So this was not something that they were prepared for at all.
Rebecca: I think we should actually take a step back, because we just launched into this conversation assuming — rightly so — that our listeners will know what the heck we’re talking about.

But for those who somehow don’t, Jensen resigned on Thursday, after it came out he was having an affair with a former executive at an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, who’s alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. And then there was another reported affair with an Nvidia executive.

So he’s resigned. Nvidia CFO Collette Kress is jumping in as the interim CEO. She’s a longtime board member. I think it’s always interesting when a CFO steps in to be a CEO. It just means we’re going to manage expenses right now, like that’s the key.

Anthony: I think a big part of the message is: This is not necessarily someone you should expect to be in this role for the long term. No disrespect to her, but it feels like a caretaker appointment while they figure things out.

Just to get into that backstory a little bit more, what has been really remarkable to me has been this sense that a lot of what ultimately brought Huang down, [that] stuff was at least known in intelligence circles for a while. Apparently, this report that [raises] questions, concerns about his relationship with Alice Huang is something that was circulating a year ago, or close to a year ago.

And then suddenly, everything really accelerated, Starting over the weekend, with Jensen Huang admitting to having an affair, the board saying it was investigating, but that it still had a lot of faith in him. And then this week, this other affair being reported on, and it just felt like there was all this bad news coming fairly quickly.

But also, it wasn’t this thing that no one had known before. I guess a lot of the general public hadn’t known. So it’s this combined feeling of, “Wow, the ground kind of shifted so quickly under him,” even though the worst stuff, the possibility that somehow national security might have been threatened, is something that actually has been known by the government for nearly a year, if not more.
Rebecca: That’s exactly right. Trump was given some warnings about Huang’s affair with someone who has ties to Chinese intelligence, potentially, and it seemed like he didn’t really mind.

I think what’s important here, though, is to note that Jensen Huang has been an advocate for loosening chip exports to China. And so this is where the crux of it is. Can anyone trust him as the CEO of this company when he’s advocating for loosening chip exports to China? Which a lot of people believe is a national security issue, because that means it will give Chinese AI companies access to our powerful chips, which will help them improve their AI, which could threaten America.

I mean, there’s two sides of this coin. And I think, honestly, that Jensen does not need a woman to tell him that — he just wants to sell more chips, and to anybody and everybody, and whether or not that’s good for national security or not, I think is honestly secondary to him.

Tim: I completely agree. I think the big turning point seems to happen on November 9 — so that would have been earlier this week, Monday, when the Bloomberg report came out and suggested that Nvidia’s head attorney had some role in inquiring about the Department of Commerce’s investigation into Alice Huang.

Things seem to have accelerated in the last few days following that. And I don’t know what role exactly that report played in it, but it seems to be maybe there was a shift within government or within the board, a kind of a daunting realization of the extent to which this had spread just beyond Jensen and some affair.

Anthony: There’s also just the question of: What does this mean for Nvidia? What does this mean for the broader AI industry? And one of the reasons those two things are very tightly connected is not just Nvidia chips themselves, but also the fact that under Jensen Huang, the company has invested very, very heavily in a number of AI startups.

People talk about the idea of an AI circular economy, and I think Nvidia has been one of the biggest players in that, in terms of both funding a lot of things, [but] also, obviously, providing the infrastructure for a lot of AI projects. So if Nvidia is going into this stage of lockdown, circle the wagons — even if it just means a small pullback, that could have really dramatic repercussions.
Rebecca: Yeah, that’s what I want to know: What happens to the Bank of Nvidia without Jensen? Is he the one leading this?

Just to throw some numbers at you, Nvidia apparently accounts for roughly 80% of the AI GPU market. It reported $99 billion in investments and another $25 billion in commitments, plus $36 billion dollars in cloud service commitments. A lot of those include investments into CoreWeave, Nebius, OpenAI, Anthropic, major data center projects. They’ve got their fingers in literally everybody’s pie.

我们没有预见到这一点。或者至少，我没有——一周前，当我写到英伟达董事会对时任首席执行官黄仁勋展开调查时，我认为他的工作是安全的。
在最新一期的 TechCrunch 股票播客中，丽贝卡·贝兰 (Rebecca Bellan)、蒂姆·德尚特 (Tim De Chant) 和我讨论了黄仁勋被罢黜的后果，以及这对更大的人工智能经济意味着什么。蒂姆说他预见到了这一点（尽管没那么快），而丽贝卡则说：“我认为这根本不会发生。”
“Jensen 是 Nvidia，对吗？”她补充道。 “而这个经济的很大一部分都依赖于英伟达。”
同样，我对黄的支持似乎崩溃得如此之快感到惊讶，而且似乎每天都有更多丑闻出现。 （与此同时，还有很多人仍然希望看到他回归。）我们也花了一些时间想知道英伟达在更大的人工智能生态系统中的投资会发生什么。
继续阅读我们的对话预览，我们的对话经过了长度和清晰度的编辑；你可以在这里收听整集。
蒂姆·德尚特（Tim De Chant）：我认为这即将到来。我没想到事情会发生得这么快。我以为至少还有几天。
丽贝卡·贝兰：我根本不认为这会发生。我的意思是，Jensen 是 Nvidia，对吗？而这个经济的很大一部分都依赖于英伟达。除了过去几年的数据之外，我们什么也没有告诉我们，亿万富翁可以为所欲为。所以令我惊讶的是，他辞职了，这几乎恢复了我对人性的信心。
但有人对我说：“如果这是埃隆，什么都不会发生。”他不会辞职。一切都不会下降
安东尼·哈：这很有趣，因为我会说，就一周前，甚至几天前，詹森与埃隆属于同一类别。我的意思是，没有人像埃隆那样特别，但它是一家非常成功的大公司。正如你所说，在很多方面，整个人工智能经济都是建立在 Nvidia 之上的。
对于大多数人来说，黄仁勋就是英伟达。他是最大股东。他有家人在公司工作，也许最重要的是，没有制定继任计划。所以这根本就不是他们有准备的事情。
丽贝卡：我认为我们实际上应该后退一步，因为我们刚刚开始这场对话时就假设——正确的是——我们的听众会知道我们到底在说什么。
但对于那些不这么认为的人来说，詹森于周四辞职，因为他与英伟达客户 Megaspeed 的前高管有染，据称该高管与中国情报部门有联系。据报道，还有另一起与英伟达高管的恋情。
所以他辞职了。 Nvidia 首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Collette Kress) 出任临时首席执行官。她是长期董事会成员。我认为当首席财务官出任首席执行官时总是很有趣。这只是意味着我们现在要管理开支，这就是关键。
安东尼：我认为这个信息的一个重要部分是：这不一定是你应该期望长期担任这个角色的人。没有对她不尊重的意思，但这感觉就像是在他们解决问题时进行的看守任命。
只是为了更深入地了解这个背景故事，对我来说真正值得注意的是这样一种感觉，即最终导致黄的很多事情至少在情报界已经知道了一段时间。显然，这份对他与黄爱丽的关系提出质疑和担忧的报道是在一年前或接近一年前流传的。
然后突然之间，一切真的加速了，从周末开始，黄仁勋承认有外遇，董事会表示正在调查，但仍然对他很有信心。然后本周，另一件事被报道，感觉所有这些坏消息都很快传来。
而且，这并不是没人知道的事情。我想很多普通民众都不知道。因此，这是一种综合的感觉，“哇，在他的领导下，形势发生了如此之快的变化”，尽管最糟糕的事情，即国家安全可能受到威胁的可能性，实际上政府已经知道了近一年，甚至更长时间。
丽贝卡：完全正确。特朗普曾就黄与可能与中国情报部门有联系的人的婚外情发出过一些警告，但他似乎并不介意。
不过，我认为这里重要的是要注意黄仁勋一直主张放宽对中国的芯片出口。这就是问题的关键所在。当他主张放松对中国的芯片出口时，有人能相信他作为这家公司的首席执行官吗？很多人认为这是一个国家安全问题，因为这意味着这将使中国人工智能公司能够使用我们强大的芯片，这将帮助他们改进人工智能，这可能会威胁到美国。
我的意思是，这枚硬币有两个方面。老实说，我认为詹森不需要一个女人来告诉他——他只是想卖更多的芯片，卖给任何人和所有人，无论这是否对国家安全有利，我认为老实说对他来说都是次要的。
蒂姆：我完全同意。我认为重大转折点似乎发生在 11 月 9 日——所以那应该是本周早些时候，也就是周一，当时彭博社的报道出来，暗示 Nvidia 的首席律师在询问商务部对 Alice Huang 的调查中发挥了一定作用。
在那之后的最后几天里，事情似乎加速了。我不知道这份报告到底在其中扮演了什么角色，但似乎政府内部或董事会内部可能发生了转变，一种令人畏惧的认识，意识到这件事已经蔓延到詹森和其他事件之外的程度。
安东尼：还有一个问题：这对 Nvidia 意味着什么？这对更广泛的人工智能行业意味着什么？这两件事紧密相连的原因之一不仅仅是英伟达芯片本身，还在于在黄仁勋的领导下，该公司对许多人工智能初创公司进行了非常非常大的投资。
人们谈论人工智能循环经济的想法，我认为英伟达是这方面最大的参与者之一，不仅为很多事情提供了资金，而且显然还为很多人工智能项目提供了基础设施。因此，如果英伟达进入这个封锁阶段，那就绕圈子——即使这只是小幅回调，也可能会产生非常戏剧性的影响。
丽贝卡：是的，这就是我想知道的：没有詹森，英伟达银行会怎样？他是领导这件事的人吗？
举几个数字，Nvidia 显然占据了 AI GPU 市场大约 80% 的份额。该公司公布了 990 亿美元的投资和另外 250 亿美元的承诺，以及 360 亿美元的云服务承诺。其中很多包括对 CoreWeave、Nebius、OpenAI、Anthropic 和主要数据中心项目的投资。他们实际上已经涉足了每个人的利益。
